tagline: A Blue Ridge livestock route carried turkeys, geese, hogs and cattle.
intro: US 74A connects Fairview with Gerton and the community of Bat Cave in Hickory Nut Gorge. At Bearwallow, the road runs between Burntshirt, Grant and Little Bearwallow mountains. North Carolina’s scenic-byway guide includes Drover’s Road among its mountain routes. Gerton lies beside Hickory Creek, while the Broad River runs through the Bat Cave community. Just northeast of Gerton, Florence Nature Preserve contains waterfalls, creeks and trails with views into the gorge.

The earlier drovers’ road was established in 1798, connecting this area with Asheville along the course followed by US 74A. Drovers moved livestock into and out of the mountains to market, mostly turkeys, with geese, hogs and cattle also making the journey. Near Fairview, Sherrill’s Inn served as an inn through much of the nineteenth century. The communities developed postal connections too: Bear Wallow’s post office opened in 1858, followed by Bat Cave in 1879 and Pump, now Gerton, in 1883.

From Fairview, US 74A leads through Gerton and Bearwallow toward Bat Cave. At Bat Cave, US 74A meets US 64 and NC 9 beside the Broad River; the combined road continues toward Chimney Rock and Lake Lure.

moments.title: Sherrill's Inn
moments.text: Sherrill’s Inn began as a log building of the saddle-bag type and was raised to two stories and covered with weatherboards. An originally separate two-story log building is attached to it. The main house is four bays wide and two deep; the attached log building measures two bays in each direction. The historic home near Fairview was built about 1845 and served as an inn through much of the nineteenth century. Its property also includes a stone spring house and a log meathouse. The inn entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.

moments.title: Gerton
moments.text: The earlier drovers’ road connected the area with Asheville in 1798, carrying market-bound livestock along the course now followed by US 74A. A water pump gave Gerton its first postal name. The Pump Post Office opened in 1883, named for the pump that supplied the valley community with water from Bearwallow Mountain. In 1902, a new postal cancelling stamp arrived with the name misspelled “Rump.” Residents chose a new name honoring teacher Gertrude Freeman, contracting her name to Gerton. The community lies on US 74A beside Hickory Creek, part of the Broad River watershed.

moments.title: Florence Nature Preserve
moments.text: Florence Nature Preserve began with a gift made in two parts. Dr. Tom and Glenna Florence donated half their interest in the 600 acres in 1996 and the remainder in 2001. The first donation made this the land trust’s first property. The land trust, now Conserving Carolina, improved nearly five miles of existing trails and opened the land as a nature preserve. Just northeast of Gerton, the preserve’s trails include views of Burnshirt Mountain from Rattlesnake Rock and Hickory Nut Gorge from Little Pisgah Point, along with waterfalls and creeks. It remains privately owned and managed by Conserving Carolina.
